messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager: HIGH - tenant 'HelmCorp' experiencing 5xxs and elevated latency from VPC-dedicated pool hc-pool-3. Auto-fallback not triggered. Alerting oncall.
oncall-miguel: I’m on it. paging now. pulling logs for hc-pool-3.
oncall-miguel: quick note — customer is on a dedicated VPC with model pin to `redwood-3b-v2` and custom KV cache settings.
sre-jun: copying me. are we seeing model OOM or infra evictions?
oncall-miguel: initial `kube` events show node evictions then increased queue latency. logs show repeated `KVCacheMiss` for tenant id `hc-tenant-42`.
eng-runtime-lead: can you paste the recent runtime error block? I want to check kernel handoff traces.
oncall-miguel: ```
2026-03-15T14:02:11Z ERROR serve/runtime: failed dispatch: model redwood-3b-v2 shard 7 OOM while allocating 1024MB
2026-03-15T14:02:13Z WARN  routing: request queue depth=124 latency_ms=5120
2026-03-15T14:02:14Z INFO  fallback: safe_variant check disabled for tenant hc-tenant-42 (pin enforced)
```
eng-runtime-lead: thanks. so it's OOMs + queue pileup. pin prevented safe variant auto-fallback.
solutions-amy: customer policy requires pin for compliance — but they allowed a fallback to `redwood-3b-quant` if node-level failures occur. that exception is only enforced via ops toggle in the customer config. I’ll check their contract.
olivia: reopening ticket INC-7321 — affected endpoints: /v1/chat, /v1/generate. Impact: elevated 5xx and timeouts, ~32% of requests returning 503 over last 20m.
dax: can we temporarily route tenant traffic to a different dedicated pool or to shared hosted while we mitigate? what's the safe option?
sre-jun: two options: 1) lift pin (tenant config) to allow safe-variant auto-fallback to `redwood-3b-quant` 2) route to spare dedicated pool hc-pool-spare (same VPC) 3) failover to hosted with data isolation note. each has compliance tradeoffs.
support-luis: customer legal wants in-VPC only, hosted fallback is a no-go. routing to spare dedicated pool is ok if we preserve tenant isolation and logs.
eng-runtime-lead: spare pool has compatible kernels but smaller memory per shard. quant variant reduces memory footprint significantly — probably safest.
oncall-miguel: proposed immediate actions: a) enable ops toggle to allow safe-variant for hc-tenant-42 (temporary) b) throttle high-cost routes to reduce queue build-up c) spin up one extra node in hc-pool-3
solutions-amy: I can message account exec and ops approvals channel. need SRE sign-off for toggle.
sre-jun: I’ll approve toggle for emergency. miguel, run the config change: `internal config set tenant:hc-tenant-42.allow_safe_variant=true --reason "emergency-oom-15mar"` and post the diff.
oncall-miguel: running now. `internal config set` applied. posting diff: ```- allow_safe_variant: false
+ allow_safe_variant: true
reason: emergency-oom-15mar``` 
incident-bot: Action log: config change applied by oncall-miguel at 2026-03-15T14:08:02Z — allow_safe_variant=true for hc-tenant-42
eng-runtime-lead: initiating canary route to `redwood-3b-quant` for 10% of traffic from hc-tenant-42. command: `route set hc-tenant-42 model redwood-3b-quant weight=10 --canary`.
oncall-miguel: canary set. monitoring metrics.
olivia: customer impact update: 503s dropped from 32% -> 12% in first 3 minutes for canary group. overall latency p95 from 4.8s -> 2.1s for canary.
dax: status on node spin-up? any evictions continuing?
sre-jun: new node joined hc-pool-3 at 14:12:40Z, but OOMs reduced after canary. queue depth trending down. no new evictions logged since 14:11.
solutions-amy: I notified customer support and account exec (cc @legal) about temporary policy change and canary. they requested audit log and duration estimate.
support-luis: informing customer via prepared note: "We've initiated a temporary safe-variant canary for a subset of traffic while we stabilize your dedicated pool. No data left the VPC. We'll revert once cluster healthy." sending now.
olivia: running postmortem checklist: capture kernel traces, KV cache hit/miss deltas, node flavors, toggles, and timeline. set retention TTL to 90d for this incident logs.
eng-runtime-lead: next steps: keep canary at 10% for 10 minutes, if stable ramp to 50% then full. if errors resurface revert immediately and route to spare pool with isolation.
oncall-miguel: at 14:20 canary → 50% per plan. metrics look good. overall 503s now 4%.
incident-bot: :white_check_mark: Incident state: mitigated -> degraded. Pager remains open for postmortem. Owners: oncall-miguel, sre-jun, eng-runtime-lead, solutions-amy.
olivia: assigning postmortem owners and ETA: draft by 2026-03-17. I'll include customer communications and contract exception rationale.
eng-runtime-lead: configuration note for follow-up: we should add an ops-safe-override that allows auto-fallback when node-level OOM rate > 3/min even if pin present. submitting RFC.
dax: please add a short-term alert: alert if pinned-tenant OOMs > 2 in 5m to trigger ops review automatically.
sre-jun: created task TSK-5492 for alert rule and RFC. linking to thread.
solutions-amy: customer accepted mitigation and wants weekly update until we finish stabilization.
oncall-miguel: closing loop with oncall handoff to night shift at 23:00 local. handoff note: canary at 50%, allow_safe_variant=true, hc-pool-3 node count +1, postmortem underway.
support-luis: added customer-facing incident summary to INC-7321 and included audit logs.
olivia: thanks team. keep thread updated for any regressions.
